column1: # What reading Scrim's code (67e0e41) found for each upstream bug, security, performance and dependency commit. Columns: hash, verdict (still-broken, fixed, n/a, unclear), port effort (S, M, L), frozen files the port touches, whether users hit it, evidence, a reproduction (described, not committed).

column6: evidence
column7: repro

column6: Ours names each custom property with css_var_of from the variable alone (crates/engine/src/codegen.rs:339, used by Tokens::var at :305 and by variable.export css at crates/engine/src/cmd/variables_io.rs:83-88), so two variables with the same name in different collections share one `--name`. Upstream added CssNames (unique per file, numeric suffix) to both.
column7: Two collections each with a colour variable `primary` (red, blue); variable.export {format: css} declares `--primary` twice and code for a layer bound to the blue one reads `var(--primary)`, which resolves to whichever came last.

column6: parse_link at crates/engine/src/cmd/comment.rs:33-36 is the pre-fix one-liner that hands the text to u64::parse, which accepts a leading '+'. Upstream checks the id is ASCII digits only.
column7: parse_link("+5") and parse_link("figcraft://comment/+5") return Some(5) instead of None.

column6: css_gradient (crates/engine/src/codegen_css.rs:86-87) prints each stop's own colour and its caller (crates/engine/src/codegen.rs:470) never passes the paint opacity, while solid paints do fold it in (:459). Upstream passes p.opacity and multiplies each stop's alpha.
column7: A frame with a black-to-x linear gradient fill at paint opacity 0.5: inspect.code css emits `#000000 0%` instead of `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.50) 0%`.

column6: text_decls writes font-family at crates/engine/src/codegen.rs:529 escaping only `"` (to `'`); backslashes, CR/LF and `<` pass through, and HTML export wraps the CSS in a <style> block (:658). Upstream escapes `\`, `"`, `<` (as \3C) and line breaks.
column7: A text layer whose font family is `A\B` or contains `</style><b>` exports CSS with a broken string, and the HTML export ends its <style> early.

column6: num at crates/engine/src/codegen.rs:107-113 rounds via v*100, which overflows to infinity for finite values above ~1.8e306, then formats `inf`; it also casts whole values with `as i64`, which saturates past 9.2e18 (a separate earlier upstream fix). There is no num6 in ours (see ca6426b9).
column7: num(1e307) returns "inf" (expected the 308-digit whole number); num(1e20) returns "9223372036854775807".

column6: Boards connectors are upstream-only: there is no crates/engine/src/boards and no connector node or tool anywhere in our engine or doc crates.

figcraft_format::add_image (crates/format/src/lib.rs:222) only reads the header dimensions, and image.place (crates/engine/src/cmd/create.rs:407), opening a PNG/JPG as a document (crates/engine/src/importers/kinds.rs:321) and widgets (crates/engine/src/widgets.rs:163) register whatever it accepts; upstream's add_readable_image decodes through the renderer first. The startup part is already handled (apps/figcraft/src/main.rs:252 launch_error), and ours has no image.replace.
column7: A PNG truncated after its IHDR chunk: image.place succeeds and draws an empty box with no message, where it should be refused as damaged.

column6: Binding the Menu key needs egui::Key::Menu, which egui 0.36.2 (our version, Cargo.toml:77) does not have; upstream relies on its egui 0.37 fork. Our keymap (crates/engine/src/keymap.rs:216, NAMED at :428) is the pre-change one, but it can't be ported without the egui upgrade.

This follows ef4c0aac: it makes library.check (which ours lacks; there is no `library.check` or allow_library) and the server library fetch refuse before falling back to the cached copy once network_refused exists. Ours has no network_refused yet, so the fallback it fixes can't happen; fold the library_server.rs hunk (our crates/engine/src/library_server.rs:150-156) into the ef4c0aac port.

With automation roots active (crates/engine/src/file_access.rs:181 confined, used by the MCP server at crates/mcp/src/server.rs:254), nothing stops a command reaching the network: Lives::start (crates/engine/src/live.rs:727), Session::net (crates/engine/src/background.rs:129-130) and refresh_server_libraries (crates/engine/src/library_server.rs:176) all only check that a link exists. Upstream adds file_access::network_refused and checks it in each.
column7: Run collab.publish {server: ...}, collab.host or plugin.directory.list inside file_access::confined(Some(roots)): the request reaches the link, where it should be refused before the link is asked.

column6: check_finite_geometry at crates/engine/src/lib.rs:911-923 still scans ds.doc.nodes() for every layer after every command; upstream walks Document::changed_ids (which ours has at crates/doc/src/lib.rs:351) instead.
column7: In a 200,000-layer document, 100 renames take about 0.6 s, against about 0.02 s with the diff (upstream's measurement).

column6: The Open link notice and proto.linkNotice are upstream-only: no link_notice or linkNotice anywhere in our engine, doc or ui-egui (and none at the fork point).

Our normalize (crates/engine/src/lib.rs:1253 onward) puts every touched layer through bindings, style links, coherent sizing, text auto-size and instance sync, with no only_moved_layers shortcut for layers whose transform alone changed.
column7: Drag 500 plain rectangles: each preview frame re-runs binding_scope, coherent_sizing and sync_after_edit for all 500, where upstream does only the parents and groups around them.

column6: file_access::read (crates/engine/src/file_access.rs:232) reads any path with no type or size check, and file.open (crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:435), image.place (crates/engine/src/cmd/create.rs:377), the image fill picker (crates/ui-egui/src/colorpicker.rs:518) and the CLI's run_script use it; read_capped (:238) also reads without a bound after checking. Our own claude_desktop.rs:379 and agent_clients.rs:539 read the same way.
column7: image.place {path: "/dev/zero"} or file.open on a FIFO hangs or fills memory, where it should be refused as not a regular file.

column6: There is no MAX_PEERS or MAX_DELETED anywhere: the collab server's deleted set only grows (crates/collab/src/server.rs:57, extended at :452), and the client keeps every peer a server announces (crates/collab-net/src/join.rs:191 clones the whole welcome list, :221 grows seen.peers).
column7: A hostile server sends a welcome listing 1,000,000 peers, or keeps sending peer-joined events: the client stores them all; a session that deletes 10^6 layers keeps 10^6 ids.

column6: doc.list (crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:240-248) returns each tab's full `path` to every caller, and plugins are explicitly allowed to call it (ALLOWED at crates/engine/src/plugins.rs:120). Upstream strips `path` for agents and plugins. Ours has no Session::agent flag, so the agent half needs our own way to tell an MCP call.
column7: A plugin calling doc.list gets ["/Users/<name>/Documents/x.figcraft"]; it should get only names.

column6: Session::grouped (crates/engine/src/lib.rs:1164-1214) lifts the history limit and lets every command inside push its own snapshot through push_undo (:476), truncating them only when the group ends. Upstream's group_step makes later edits in a group reuse the step it already pushed.
column7: In a grouped closure running 1,000 node.set renames, history.undo.len() reaches base+1000 during the group, where it should stay at base+1.

column6: Test-only commit; the behaviour it pins is broken in ours because Session::grouped (crates/engine/src/lib.rs:1164) has no catch_unwind (see 9573b8b2), so a panic skips the live_hold(false) calls (:1177-1179) and the original payload is never re-raised by a rollback.
column7: In a hosted live session, grouped(|s| { node.set; panic!() }) under catch_unwind leaves the document edited and held, and a later node.set never goes out.

column6: Variables::get and Variables::collection (crates/doc/src/styles.rs:267-273) match an id or a name, and resolve (:277-285) and the other stored-reference lookups use them, so a stored id can resolve to a different variable or collection whose name equals it. Upstream adds get_by_id/collection_by_id and uses them for stored references across 34 files.
column7: Collections `c` and a second one with id "shadow" named "c" listed first: resolving a variable of `c` takes the shadow collection's modes and falls back to the wrong value; renaming a variable to another's id hides an alias cycle from variable.set.

column6: Session::grouped (crates/engine/src/lib.rs:1164-1214) calls f(self) bare, so a panic in the closure outside a command skips the rollback: documents stay half edited, history.limit stays usize::MAX and live documents stay held. The MCP server catches the unwind (crates/mcp/src/server.rs:254) and carries on with that state.
column7: grouped("G", |s| { s.execute("node.set", rename)?; panic!() }) under catch_unwind: the rename stays and history.limit is usize::MAX.

column6: variables_param (crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:588-596) reads a `variables` path with the uncapped read (:435), so no type or size limit applies. Upstream reads it with read_capped(path, 256 MiB).
column7: variable.import {variables: "/dev/zero"} hangs or fills memory, where it should be refused.

column6: layout_add (crates/engine/src/cmd/structure.rs:540-545) sorts all children by position, masks included, so a mask moves away from the layers it clips; infer_layout (:493-496) also measures hidden and absolute children. The in-place group conversion and Fill-sizing half is n/a: ours wraps groups in a new frame.
column7: A frame with [mask circle at x=100, image at x=0] and Add auto layout (layout.add): the image sorts ahead of the mask and stops being masked.

column6: Only direct self-containment is refused (create_instance_at at crates/engine/src/components.rs:268, instance.place at crates/engine/src/cmd/component.rs:274), and sync_instance_depth stops only when an instance is inside its own main (components.rs:565) or past MAX_DEPTH 16 (:40). Indirect loops are accepted, and files holding them aren't repaired on open.
column7: Component A, component B containing an instance of A, then component.instance of B with parent A: it is accepted, and an instance of A on the page expands A>B>A… to 16 levels (exponentially with two nested instances per level).

column6: node.set reads isMask, wrap, strokesIncluded, reverseZ, constrainProportions and sectionContentsHidden with as_bool().unwrap_or(false) (crates/engine/src/cmd/props.rs:467, 543, 553, 554, 651, 816), so a non-boolean silently becomes false.
column7: node.set {isMask: "true"} on a mask layer succeeds and turns the mask off, where it should be refused with "`isMask` must be a boolean".

column6: css_safe (crates/engine/src/cmd/variables_io.rs:62-63) neutralises `"`, `\` and LF but not CR or form feed.
column7: A string variable whose value contains "\r" exports as a CSS string with a raw CR (an invalid string token).

column6: set_paint_color (crates/engine/src/cmd/styles.rs:1114) adds the first bound paint with Paint::solid(c), which moves the colour's alpha into the opacity, and rebind_paint_alpha (:800) can't reset it because no paint existed at bind time. The next apply then writes the full colour into the kind (:1113) and the alpha counts twice.
column7: A rectangle with no fills bound to colour variable #0D6EFD80: after any later edit of the layer its effective fill alpha is about 0.25 instead of 0.5.

column6: This widens d4471376's Frame-only check on the thumbnail layer; ours has no selected-frame thumbnail at all (see d4471376), and our object.setThumbnail (crates/engine/src/cmd/structure.rs:81-92) accepts any layer. Use is_frame_like when porting d4471376.
The fix is in paint_paste (fill.paste/stroke.paste), which ours doesn't have: no paint_paste or clipboard paint_images; we only have edit.pasteProperties (crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs:708).
Same paint_paste image-key code as 1c253ef3; fill.paste/stroke.paste are not in ours.
Same paint_paste image-key code as 1c253ef3; fill.paste/stroke.paste are not in ours.

This fixes review issues in upstream PR #1457 (release narrowing to the clicked layer or label in canvas/tools/drag.rs, reorder rings in selection_spacing). Ours has neither: the press code at crates/engine/src/tools.rs:1207-1221 has no `keep`/label narrowing, and there is no Reorder action in ui-egui.

The ArkUI half is n/a (no ArkUI target). In the canvas half, our input (crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs:491, dispatch at :621-650) sends PointerKind::Down at the frame's hover_pos rather than the press event's own position. Ours also never sends the same-frame release that upstream added post-fork (2a3c5b46).
column7: Inject PointerButton{pressed:true} at (10,10) then PointerMoved to (40,10) in one egui frame with the Move tool: the press reaches the tools at (40,10), so the hit and the drag start are taken at the wrong point.

column6: scale_node (crates/engine/src/cmd/arrange.rs:397 onward) never marks size/position overrides, and our override recording drops geometry that changed while an ancestor resized (geometry_derived, crates/engine/src/components.rs:1072-1078). So a scaled instance's inner layers lose their scale on the next rebuild.
column7: Instance of a 24 px icon component; transform.scale the instance by 14/24; add a layer to the main: the instance's inner shape returns to 24 px.

column6: The text auto-size step of our normalize (crates/engine/src/lib.rs:1286-1293) calls set_size with the origin fixed, and nothing anchors right-aligned auto-width text (no keeps_right_edge; TextAlignH::Right appears only in codegen and inspect).
column7: Auto-width text aligned right at x=100, width 50, not in auto layout: set its characters longer and its left edge stays at 100 and the right edge moves out, where the right edge should stay at 150.

column6: execute runs only the command under guard::run (crates/engine/src/lib.rs:859); normalize runs afterwards in after_command (:966) unguarded, and the text preview normalises outside the guard too (crates/engine/src/textpreview.rs:42). A panic while normalising therefore unwinds past the rollback.
column7: With a normalize step forced to panic, any edit command unwinds out of execute and leaves the document half normalised and with no undo step, instead of returning EngineError::Internal with the edit rolled back.

column6: page.duplicate (crates/engine/src/cmd/page.rs:96) takes `id` unchecked, while the other page commands go through page_target (:28-34), which refuses non-pages.
column7: page.duplicate {id: <a frame's id>} adds a page "Copy of Frame" holding copies of the frame's children, where it should be refused with "is not a page".

column6: paddingHorizontal and paddingVertical use f64_of(v).unwrap_or(0.0) (crates/engine/src/cmd/props.rs:522 and :528), unlike paddingTop and the rest (:516), which refuse.
column7: node.set {paddingHorizontal: "abc"} on an auto layout frame with padding 16 succeeds and sets left/right padding to 0.

column6: MCP tool arguments aren't checked against the tool schemas (crates/mcp/src/tools.rs:546 dispatch), and command.batch reads only command/params from each step (crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs:336-337), ignoring other keys. This doesn't depend on ff4fe002.
column7: MCP run_command {command: "node.delete", args: {ids: [x]}} runs node.delete on the current selection with no params, where it should be refused for the unknown `args`.

column6: Session::execute (crates/engine/src/lib.rs:859) runs commands with whatever keys they get; there is no param_names/refuse_unknown_params, so misspelt parameters are silently ignored. Porting means parsing our own params docs (which differ from upstream's) and fixing tests that pass extra keys.
column7: comment.list {filterr: "open"} succeeds and lists resolved threads too, where it should be refused naming `filterr`.

column6: apply's key order (crates/engine/src/cmd/props.rs:322-327) gives `layout` the same rank as every tuning key, so serde_json's alphabetical map order decides: an object `layout` (:500) replaces a gap set before it, and padding after `layout: null` turns auto layout back on.
column7: node.set {gap: 24, layout: {mode: "vertical"}} ends with the default gap; node.set {layout: null, padding: 8} leaves auto layout on.

column6: crates/render/src/fx.rs is byte-identical to upstream's pre-image (same md5): the row-by-row bounds-checked box_blur_h and O(r) morph that the commit replaces. Our render crate already depends on rayon.
column7: Exporting the examples' top-level frames as PNG/JPG/WebP at 2x takes about twice as long as upstream after the change (7.0 s against 3.6 s in its benchmark).

column6: object.setThumbnail tags a layer with figcraft.thumbnail (crates/engine/src/cmd/structure.rs:81-92), but thumbnail() (crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:701-713) always renders the first page's whole content and never reads the tag. figcraft_render::Options::solo, which upstream uses, already exists in ours.
column7: Two frames on page 1; Set as thumbnail on the second, then save: the file's thumbnail.png shows both frames, not the chosen one.

column6: color_of (crates/engine/src/params.rs:169-176) filter_maps away non-numeric entries before matching the length, so a malformed array can become a different valid colour.
column7: color_of([1, 0, 0, "x"]) returns opaque red and color_of([1, "x", 0, 0]) returns rgb(1, 0, 0); both should be None.

column6: node.set opacity (crates/engine/src/cmd/props.rs:392-395) divides by 100 only when the value is above 1, and f64_of drops a `%` suffix (crates/engine/src/params.rs:17), so small percentages read as fractions.
column7: node.set {opacity: "1%"} gives opacity 1.0 (should be 0.01); {opacity: "0.5%"} gives 0.5.

column6: A failed group restores the redo stack but only truncates the undo stack to its old length (crates/engine/src/lib.rs:1185-1195), so undo steps that an edit.undo inside the group popped are lost.
column7: Edit A; command.batch [edit.undo, a failing step]: the batch fails and the document is back, but A's undo step is gone (undo depth one lower than before).

column6: node.find was added upstream after the fork; ours has no node.find command (our layer search is node.query, crates/engine/src/cmd/query/).
four() (crates/engine/src/cmd/props.rs:117-130), used by cornerRadius, padding and strokeSides arrays, filter_maps away non-numeric entries, so a junk array can collapse to a valid shorter one.
column7: node.set {padding: [10, "abc"]} sets [10,10,10,10]; [10, "abc", null, 20] sets [10,20,10,20]; both should be refused.

column6: The Dart variable export is upstream-only: our variable.export takes json|css only (crates/engine/src/cmd/variables_io.rs:47-50).
The Dart variable export is upstream-only: our variable.export takes json|css only (crates/engine/src/cmd/variables_io.rs:47-50).

It refines behind_sel, upstream's 'a press inside the selection drags it' logic from 795567f0 (#910, 21 Oct, after the fork). Ours has no behind_sel; our press handling (crates/engine/src/tools.rs:1207-1221) only keeps a multi-selection when the hit target is in it.

Same post-fork behind_sel code as 45326b3b (from upstream 795567f0, #910), which ours lacks. Ours doesn't drag a selected unfilled shape from inside its box at all, which is the missing #910 feature rather than this bug.

Our layout applies max_lines only to Truncate (crates/text/src/layout.rs:504), the ellipsis follows the last whole word, and an explicit height turns truncating text into fixed (crates/engine/src/cmd/props.rs:373). There is no TextData::truncates/fix_size (crates/doc/src/text.rs).
column7: Truncating text with 2 max lines, then node.set {height: 40}: auto_resize becomes None and the ellipsis is gone; auto-height text with maxLines 2 ignores the limit.

column6: It reorders a648700f's on-disk stamp (taken before the read); ours has no stamp at all (see a648700f). Take the stamp before reading when porting a648700f.

DocState keeps no on-disk stamp, and save (crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:831) and save_to (:810) write over the file whatever happened to it since open (:656). library.rs has the private Stamp/stat that upstream reuses.
column7: Open x.figcraft, change it from another process (figcraft-cli run --out x.figcraft, a sync client), then file.save: it reports saved and the other change is lost, where it should be refused unless overwrite: true.

column6: lengths_to_rem writes `num(v / root)` (crates/engine/src/codegen.rs:180), and num rounds to 2 decimals, so rem values don't convert back to the same pixels.
column7: inspect.code css with unit rem and a 13px font size gives 0.81rem (12.96 px) instead of 0.8125rem.

column6: It corrects 0a4e70fb's step-naming (which turned BadParams into Other); ours has neither. Port its final form (EngineError::at_step) when porting 0a4e70fb.

It removes a loop in Face that forces opsz to the text size, which upstream added with its own Sketch import (ad78ee94, 21 Oct); our crates/text/src/fontdb.rs never had it, and our Sketch importer is our own.
It narrows refuse_dropping_images in save_to, which came with c305e23a; ours has neither (see c305e23a).

It hardens c305e23a's same_file and run-script check (hard links via the same-file crate); ours has no same_file in crates/engine/src/file_access.rs and no images-past-budget guard. Fold it into the c305e23a port.

load_within (crates/format/src/lib.rs:498) leaves out images past IMAGE_BUDGET (4 GiB / 20,000, :74) and only reports them, and nothing remembers that, so save writes the archive from memory and drops them.
column7: A .figcraft whose images exceed 4 GiB: open it, then file.save onto the same path, and the images left out are gone from the file for good, where the save should be refused.

column6: batch_step (crates/engine/src/lib.rs:1157-1160) returns the failing command's error as is; only $step resolution errors name the step. Port with 6f1999c2's at_step so the error kind is kept.
column7: command.batch [rect, node.set {id: 999}]: the error says the node is missing but not that step 1 failed.

column6: scale_node scales a vector network with VectorNetwork::scale (crates/engine/src/cmd/arrange.rs:491-492, crates/doc/src/vector.rs:597-606), which moves vertices and tangents but leaves each vertex's corner radius (vector.rs:42).
column7: A vector with a 10 px rounded vertex, transform.scale by 2: the shape doubles but the vertex radius stays 10 (should be 20).

column6: RESERVED in crates/engine/src/component_codegen.rs:226 lacks arguments, await, eval, implements and protected (await appears only in RUST_RESERVED at :365), so props with those names become illegal strict-mode parameter names.
column7: A component with a boolean property named "Protected" generates a JSX/TS component whose parameter is `protected`, a syntax error in strict-mode JS.

column6: Our text.onPath (crates/engine/src/cmd/text.rs:127 on_path) never moves the path layer's fills or effects (or their style links) to the text; upstream added that transfer after the fork, and this fix only corrects it.

crates/engine/src/codegen.rs:112 num() still formats whole values with an i64 cast, which saturates at 2^63. Only a layer value of about 9.2e18 or more (an agent setting an absurd x or width) reaches it.
column7: Unit test in codegen.rs: num(1e20) returns 9223372036854775807 and num(-1e20) returns -9223372036854775808 instead of 100000000000000000000 and its negative.

column6: crates/engine/src/cmd/arrange.rs:202-203 distribute() still measures the span to the right/bottom edge of the layer that starts last, not the outermost edge. When a wide layer sorted earlier reaches past the last one, the gap comes out too small or negative and the layers are pulled together (also arrange.packH/packV).
column7: Select A (x 0..10), B (x 20..200), C (x 50..60), run arrange.distributeH: the gap is (60-200)/2 = -70 so the layers overlap; expected the span 0..200 and a gap of 0.

column6: crates/engine/src/cmd/layout.rs:41 set_track() bounds the index by the stored grid_columns/grid_rows (a u32 serde reads unclamped from a file) and then resizes the track list to index+1; only the layout pass caps at MAX_TRACKS (crates/layout/src/lib.rs:611). A crafted file can make it allocate billions of tracks.
column7: Set a grid frame's grid_columns to 5_000_000 directly in the doc, run layout.setTrack {axis: columns, index: 4999999, sizing: hug}: it succeeds and column_tracks has 5,000,000 entries; expected an error and at most 1000 tracks.

column6: Session::execute (crates/engine/src/lib.rs:858-894) rolls back doc, selection and page on a refused command but not self.clipboard, so edit.cut writes the clipboard and keeps it after check_preview/check_live_access/check_instance_structure refuse the cut. lib.rs is frozen at exactly 1773 lines, so the two added lines need an offset.
column7: Copy layer B, open version.preview {index:0}, run edit.cut on layer A: the cut is refused (Disabled) but the clipboard now holds A instead of B.

column6: crates/text/src/fontdb.rs:723-728 system_font_dirs() on Linux/BSD still scans only /usr/share/fonts, /usr/local/share/fonts and the user folders, never $XDG_DATA_DIRS, /run/host/fonts or the folders fontconfig names. Our figcraft-text has no craft-font-catalog dependency (crates/text/Cargo.toml), so the port means adding it (a dependency-log entry) or parsing fonts.conf ourselves.
column7: On NixOS or Guix (fonts only under the fontconfig/XDG_DATA_DIRS folders), the font list shows only the bundled faces: system families such as DejaVu are missing.

column6: crates/render/src/draw.rs:170 stroke_area() still takes the even-odd ring fast path for every closed outside stroke without dashes, profile or brush; the outer ring is a square-cornered rectangle, so a Round or Bevel join on a sharp corner draws as a miter.
column7: A 100x100 rectangle with no corner radius, an Outside 20 px stroke and join Round: the pixel at the outer corner (-19,-19) is painted; expected it clear (rounded corner), as with the generic stroker.

column6: crates/pathops/src/lib.rs:288-290 stroke_center() applies the dash pattern from offset 0 over the whole path, and width.rs variable_outline/dashes do the same, so an open dashed line starts with a full dash and ends wherever the pattern falls; there is no line_dashes/subpath_dashes fitting. The port also touches SVG export (lib.rs stroke writer) and import (crates/svg/src/import/mod.rs:444 stroke_props).
column7: A 100 px open line with dashes [10,10]: ours paints 0..10, 20..30 ... 80..90 and leaves the end bare; expected a half dash 0..5 and 95..100 with whole patterns scaled to fit, as Figma draws it.

column6: crates/text/src/fontdb.rs:653 fallbacks_for() still calls find() for each of the 20 FALLBACK_FAMILIES, and find() (line 595) loads every pending face of the family, with file bytes shared only within one family (load_family, line 575). Our FontDb has no generation counter, so upstream's per-style fallback cache (FallbackLists) and cross-family file sharing need reworking rather than a straight copy.
column7: On Linux with Noto Sans CJK installed, lay out one Latin text: all CJK collection files (about 7 files, over 100 MB) are read into memory, the SC and KR faces twice; expected only the nearest face per family.

column6: The bug is in normal_track (trak table tracking), which our crates/text/src/fontdb.rs does not have (no trak reading at all). The other half only makes index_bytes (fontdb.rs:795) bounds explicit; ours has the same shape but every addition is already bounded by fill() checking the range first, as upstream notes, and the folder scan does not run on wasm32.

crates/text/src/layout.rs:315-323 layout() still dedupes spans into styles with styles.iter().position, a linear scan per span, so a text with many distinct runs costs O(spans x styles) full TextStyle comparisons on every layout. layout.rs is frozen at 1323 lines, so the fingerprint buckets have to live in a new module.

column7: A fig-kiwi canvas whose schema has a message of 64 uint fields, repeated so the message is 400 MB of one-byte scalars, deflated to a few MB: it decodes about 400M Kv values instead of failing with "too many values".

column7: A .scrim zip with a member images/../evil: load_bytes keeps an image under hash "../evil" instead of reporting it as unread.

column7: Title-case text "say 'hi'": the canvas shows "Say 'hi'" instead of "Say 'Hi'".

column7: A document with a node whose x is f64::NAN, saved with save_bytes and reopened with load_bytes: it fails with "invalid type: null, expected f64" instead of opening with x = 0.

column7: A vector ring (two concentric loops, one region with WindingRule::EvenOdd): a click in the hole selects the vector, though nothing is painted there.
